items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: And she can tell you because we practice a lot.

ctx.x: I don’t feel bad about it because he is. But it just seems like as he’s getting older people are reacting to his playing in a more emotional way, that a lot of times you have people, like, in tears. You know, just teary eyed. And they can’t believe what they’re hearing. And I think that for us baby boomers and people that are around our age group, it gives us some kind of like hope for ourselves that maybe we’ll, well hopefully we can be in a place — it kind of shows people what you’re capable of in old age. I…

Yesterday I was listening to an interview with George Clooney. And he was talking about Rosemary Clooney, who was his aunt I think, and how she in her later career made different musical choices because her voice had changed a lot. Do you find that you need to make different musical choices when you’re improvising now?
